title: Which Case? Pairing be-/ki- with -ba/-be and -ból/-ből

sections.title: The prefix and the case suffix point the same way
sections.content: You already know -ba/-be ('into') and -ból/-ből ('out of') from A1. With bemegy/bejön and kimegy/kijön, the prefix and the case suffix have to agree: be- pairs with -ba/-be, and ki- pairs with -ból/-ből. Leave either one out and the sentence sounds unfinished — the prefix says which way, the case suffix says which place.

items.english: I'm going out of the shop.
Gábor gets out of the car.

sections.content: Don't reach for -ban/-ben here — that's the case for just being somewhere (a boltban, 'in the shop'), with no motion at all. bemegy and kimegy are both about movement, so they always take a directional case, -ba/-be or -ból/-ből, never the plain locative.
